about: Real recordings of the V-22 Osprey, for its sounds (owner, 19 Nov 2026: a real, named machine may sound like itself from real recordings; assets/AGENTS.md). Every source is a DVIDS video marked PUBLIC DOMAIN on its page, made by US service members in their official duties. Credit each by name, and say that the appearance of US Department of Defense visual information does not imply or constitute DoD endorsement. Cuts and roles are the agent's first reading (19 Nov 2026) from spectrograms and a frame every 10 seconds, for the owner to judge on the listening page; nothing here is picked.
licence: Public domain (US federal government work), per each DVIDS page; DVIDS asks for credit and the no-endorsement line

978528.title: America's Air Show 2025 B-Roll Day 1: MV-22B Osprey Demo
978528.credit: Lance Cpl. Brooke Pedersen and Lance Cpl. Madison Luciano, US Marine Corps
978528.seen: 0 to 10 s a close hover pass; then the demonstration further off

875555.title: CV-22 Osprey Tiltrotor Aircraft B-Roll
875555.credit: Staff Sgt. Candin Muniz and Airman 1st Class Alexis Sandoval, US Air Force
875555.seen: 57 to 65 s on the ground with rotors turning, outside; 73 to 145 s inside the cabin, ending with the engines winding down on a runway

586454.title: CV-22 Osprey taxi 1
586454.credit: Senior Airman Timothy Kirchner, US Air Force
586454.seen: 15 s taxiing; a steady blade-pass comb near 19.7 Hz

1007376.title: U.S. Air Force CV-22 Osprey demonstrates capabilities during Japanese-American Friendship Festival 2026
1007376.credit: 374th Airlift Wing Public Affairs, US Air Force
1007376.seen: 0 to 60 s and 140 to 270 s inside the cabin with the ramp open; 120 to 135 s and the end hovering over a crowd

968286.title: USS Iwo Jima Flight Operations with MV-22B Osprey
968286.credit: Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Joseph T. Miller, US Navy
968286.seen: a landing, then deck work; blades folded by 30 s; deck noise and another aircraft's tone

791592.title: MV-22B Osprey Flight Operations Aboard USNS Mercy
791592.credit: Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Luke Cunningham, US Navy
791592.seen: a night approach and landing on deck (touchdown near 58 s), then rotors turning on deck
